chunks: And everything in it that is narrated from Abu Khadijah Salim ibn Makram Al-Jammal, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah have mercy on him - from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi Al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadijah Salim ibn Makram Al-Jammal.

key_terms.الْجَمَّالِ: Al-Jammal (the jeweler, a nisba indicating profession or origin)
key_terms.سَالِمِ بْنِ مَكْرَمَ: Salim ibn Makram (personal name and father's name)
key_terms.عَمِّهِ: His uncle (referring to the uncle of Majilawayh)

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator in the chain for Abu Khadijah Salim ibn Makram Al-Jammal in this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous approach to verifying the authenticity of narrations by explicitly tracing the chain back to Abu Khadijah Salim ibn Makram Al-Jammal. By detailing the specific transmission route through Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh and his contemporaries, al-Saduq underscores the reliability of the *Ahl al-Bayt* tradition within the broader context of early Shia hadith scholarship.
